races.name: QuinnBet Best Odds Guaranteed 'Confined' Handicap

runners_data.name: Leonato
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile for trainer George Boughey, 36 days since last run which could mean freshness or rustiness; best form came over shorter and his last three runs are modest, so the step to 1m6f on good ground is an open question despite Jack Callan's claiming allowance.|

runners_data.name: Kelly Burn
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon partners this James Fanshawe-trained filly who has shown front-running form at 12f on Standout ground — uncontested today she gets her ideal scenario, though the STYLE_FIT flag notes she can be pushed wider than this role; a win last time out over this trip suggests stamina is confirmed.|

runners_data.name: Mountbatten
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's horses are notoriously well-timed and this three-year-old arrives just eight days after winning over 12f on Standout — the stable rarely runs horses back so quickly without strong confidence; a hold-up style suits this shape if Kelly Burn sets a fair clip, though being beaten into seven-lengths finishes at 7f-8f suggests he needed time and distance to find his game.|

runners_data.name: Queen Of Astolat
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes filly whose genuine hold-up nature means she's positioned on the map in midfield rather than her natural position at the rear — she has shown just two placings from five runs and carries the lowest weight in the race; the STYLE_FIT discount is real given she may struggle to get into the race from her true position if the pace is slow.|

races.paceDynamic: Kelly Burn is the sole confirmed front-runner in this four-runner field and, with no rival likely to challenge for the lead, she should slot into an uncontested, comfortable gallop on Good to Firm ground over 1m6f. Mountbatten and Leonato are both hold-up types who will sit behind and wait for a signal, while Queen Of Astolat — a true hold-up horse redistributed to midfield on the map — is unlikely to be up competing for position early in this shape. With Kelly Burn controlling tempo alone, she sets a sustainable, honest pace that will test the stamina of those coming from off it, but without a true pressurer to force her hand the fractions may be measured rather than searching. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a decisive finishing kick — particularly Mountbatten and Leonato — who can track a lone leader into the straight and pounce on a potentially moderate gallop, provided they have the turn of foot to get past Kelly Burn when the moment arrives.

scenarios.title: Controlled Solo Lead Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Kelly Burn dictates a measured gallop and the hold-up horses fail to accelerate convincingly on Good to Firm ground.
scenarios.body: If Kelly Burn dictates a measured gallop and the hold-up horses fail to accelerate convincingly on Good to Firm ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Kelly Burn's controlled tempo is honest enough to stretch the field and one hold-up runner produces a sharp turn of foot in the straight.
scenarios.body: If Kelly Burn's controlled tempo is honest enough to stretch the field and one hold-up runner produces a sharp turn of foot in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Two Closers Hit Line Together
scenarios.trigger: If both Mountbatten and Leonato time their challenges identically and Kelly Burn ties up in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If both Mountbatten and Leonato time their challenges identically and Kelly Burn ties up in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos Ensues
scenarios.trigger: If Kelly Burn blazes an unexpectedly fast pace and ties up before the final furlong, leaving the race wide open.
scenarios.body: If Kelly Burn blazes an unexpectedly fast pace and ties up before the final furlong, leaving the race wide open.

watchPoints.text: Watch Kelly Burn's early fractions — if Cieren Fallon allows her to coast through the first mile unchallenged, she could prove very difficult to reel in on this Good to Firm surface with hold-up horses unable to close the gap quickly enough.

Mountbatten's rapid turnaround (8 days) is typical Prescott confidence but warrants monitoring — if he bounces off the quick return he could underperform despite having the most compelling profile for this race shape.

Leonato's form over shorter trips (8f-10f) and mixed recent figures raise a stamina concern at 1m6f; Jack Callan's 3lb claim helps but watch whether he simply runs out of race in the final two furlongs.

Queen Of Astolat's sim-going record on Good (2 runs, 0 wins, 0 places) is a soft caution — she has not shown she handles this surface, and in a race where the pace shape already disadvantages her true hold-up style, this adds a secondary layer of doubt.

With only four runners the race is very unlikely to split into tactical factions — any horse slow away or awkward at the start could find itself impossibly detached in a small-field, steady-gallop scenario; monitor the gates closely at the off.

races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Gorgeous Mr George
runners_data.note: Consistent if well-beaten sort in competitive handicaps, but this restricted maiden is a significant drop in class; has form on similar going, jockey Taryn Langley claims 5lb, and a prominent position from the off suits his style — he is a credible player to place.

runners_data.name: Distinct Spirit
runners_data.note: Long absence of 263 days is the immediate concern here; has winning form on good ground at seven furlongs but her natural instinct to race prominently may be compromised by the number of horses ahead of her in this field, meaning she could race in an uncharacteristic midfield slot.

runners_data.name: Daring Legend
runners_data.note: Predominantly a six-to-seven-furlong horse stepping up to a mile; the headgear change (tongue tie) is noted and her hold-up style will require a strong pace to be set to get competitive — she is a wait-and-see runner.

runners_data.name: North View
runners_data.note: Veteran handicapper who holds up and needs things to happen in front of her; the step back to a mile on Good to Firm from Standard tracks is a positive, but her recent form figures include a seven and a thirteen, suggesting she needs everything to fall right.

runners_data.name: Berry Clever
runners_data.note: In good recent form with a win at seven furlongs and a runner-up, but she races off a style that wants to be prominent — the congested pace map means she is likely pushed back from her ideal pitch, and her best chance depends on reclaiming that forward berth mid-race.

runners_data.name: Ya Karim
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner and confirmed pace-setter with a win on good ground; has the highest OR in the field and the licence to dictate entirely at her own tempo — the STYLE_FIT tag reminds that a moderate gallop may not test opponents sufficiently, but her class edge is real.

runners_data.name: Luzon Heights
runners_data.note: Consistent performer at a mile with multiple placed efforts on similar ground; Cieren Fallon is a significant booking and the horse's record of 1-2-2-4-5 from five starts shows genuine ability — well positioned to sit just off Ya Karim and challenge in the straight.

runners_data.name: Peel Park
runners_data.note: Roger Varian-trained three-year-old who has found it tough in better company; all eight of her runs have come on Good ground and she handles the surface, but her form figures of 5-7-6-6-16 suggest she needs to find improvement to be competitive here.

runners_data.name: Kaori
runners_data.note: George Boughey has a strong recent strike rate (7/34 in 14 days) and the drop from Listed-level company to this restricted maiden represents a class relief; however, she is a hold-up filly whose single run on good ground was a fourth, and she will need more pace ahead of her than this field may generate.

races.paceDynamic: Ya Karim is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival likely to dispute the lead aggressively, she should dictate comfortably from the front on Good to Firm ground over a mile at Yarmouth. Gorgeous Mr George and Luzon Heights will press forward to track her, creating a controlled, honest pace rather than a frantic gallop — the kind of tempo that rewards those able to travel prominently without burning fuel. Distinct Spirit and Berry Clever are natural prominent types who would ordinarily race close to the pace, but with Ya Karim, Gorgeous Mr George, Luzon Heights, and Peel Park all ahead of them on the map, they are more likely to find themselves shuffled into mid-division than to secure their natural position; Ya Karim and Luzon Heights are best placed to hold the rail berths. This race shape — a single uncontested leader setting a steady, measured gallop — overwhelmingly favours prominent racers who can sit just off the pace and pounce from a handy position in the straight, with deep closers likely to find the final two furlongs too short to reel in those who have travelled comfortably throughout.

scenarios.title: Ya Karim Dictates Freely
scenarios.trigger: If Ya Karim leads uncontested at a comfortable clip and holds her shape into the Yarmouth straight.
scenarios.body: If Ya Karim leads uncontested at a comfortable clip and holds her shape into the Yarmouth straight.

scenarios.title: Pace Collapses; Closers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is so slow that the field concertinas, giving hold-up horses a genuine shot at the prize.
scenarios.body: If the gallop is so slow that the field concertinas, giving hold-up horses a genuine shot at the prize.

scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage Mid-Race

scenarios.body: If Distinct Spirit or Berry Clever push forward to reclaim their natural positions, increasing pressure on Ya Karim through the middle part of the race.

scenarios.title: Front Runner Fades; Chaser Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Ya Karim hits the front two early and burns out, leaving the door open for a late-developing chaser.

watchPoints.text: Ya Karim's sectional fractions — if she is allowed to coast in front unchallenged through the first half-mile, she could prove very hard to catch for any hold-up horse in this field.

Distinct Spirit and Berry Clever: watch how quickly they break and whether they push forward to claim a prominent position, because if both do, the pace dynamic changes materially and the mid-race tempo lifts.

Luzon Heights with Cieren Fallon — if Fallon slots her directly behind Ya Karim in second or third, she becomes the most dangerous challenger in the straight given her strong mile form on this ground.

North View and Kaori are both hold-up types who need a searching pace; if the race is run at a crawl, neither will be able to produce a winning challenge from the back, so monitor early fractions for the viability of their tactics.
Peel Park wears a hood (b) — watch her behaviour in the stalls and whether she settles cleanly in the early stages, as a poor break from a prominent draw could compromise her race entirely.

races.name: Winning Experience With Moulton Racing Handicap

runners_data.name: Rokuni
runners_data.note: Charlie Wallis's 4yo has a dismal recent record (9th, 11th, 12th among recent runs) on varying surfaces, and though Good going is not flagged as a concern, the horse is a true hold-up type squeezed into midfield by the congested rear; the 1/4 T14 record is modest, and nothing in recent form suggests a reversal is imminent.

runners_data.name: Shabu Shabu
runners_data.note: James Ferguson's 4yo has a solid foundation of 10f form on Good ground (2nd from two relevant starts) and the 62-day freshener is not necessarily a negative for a horse with prior form; Harry Vigors takes the 5lb claim, and as a hold-up type with genuine staying profile this trip suits better than most rivals.

runners_data.name: Sunset In Paris
runners_data.note: An 8yo veteran for J R Jenkins returning after 101 days — jockey has been off 46 days too — and a true hold-up horse placed into midfield on the map because the rear is congested; the stable's low 0/7 T14 strike rate flags indifference, and recent All-Weather form at 10f has been uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Zafaan
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up specialist who has contested staying distances on Good ground with credit (2nd at 16f, 3rd at 17f) but is stepping sharply back in trip to 10f and returning from 302 days off — an 8/15 similar-going record with one win suggests the conditions suit, yet the layoff and trip contraction make confidence difficult.

runners_data.name: Hunting Berries
runners_data.note: Chris Dwyer's 3yo has finished 10th, 11th and 12th in three starts and carries a fade flag; mapped to midfield from a true hold-up position, the horse has shown no evidence of handling any surface at this stage, and at OR 36 this is a very low-class runner with limited prospects regardless of shape.

runners_data.name: Ibiza Lights
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's 3yo is fitted with a visor and handled by De Sousa, which suggests the yard is trying to activate latent ability; however, the fade flag and an 8th finish in the sole Good-ground run are uninspiring, and this natural hold-up horse is poorly served by a race that will likely reward those travelling prominently.

runners_data.name: Mist Of Time
runners_data.note: William Knight's second string in this race — sharing a trainer with Raise The Stakes creates an interesting stable dynamic — and carries the fade flag after an 8th on the All-Weather most recently; as a horse who may travel close to the stable companion, its chance hinges entirely on whether it can sustain the effort into the straight.

runners_data.name: Raise The Stakes
runners_data.note: Recent runner for William Knight — returned just 8 days ago — and is the only realistic pace-setter in this field despite being a natural prominent type; Good-to-Firm ground suits horses who can bowl along freely, and Cieren Fallon's assured front-running experience makes this redistribution to the lead entirely credible, though the fade flag is a concern in the final furlong.

races.paceDynamic: Raise The Stakes is the only confirmed pace-setter in this 1m2f handicap, redistributed to the lead from a natural prominent position, and will almost certainly dictate from the front on what the going report confirms is Good To Firm ground — faster than the declared Going of Good. With just one horse likely to set the pace, the tempo will be controlled and sustainable rather than pressured, creating a single-file procession that strongly favours those who can travel close to the pace and quicken from a handy position. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Zafaan, Ibiza Lights, Sunset In Paris, Rokuni and Hunting Berries are all genuine hold-up horses competing for the same late ground, and only those who can adjust forward toward the pace or travel smoothly through a compressed midfield will be best placed. This shape overwhelmingly favours horses with tactical versatility who can sit just off Raise The Stakes and land a challenge in the straight, rather than true closers who will be stuck in traffic waiting for a run that may never come.

scenarios.body: If Raise The Stakes sets a steady, unchallenged gallop and the field strings out behind in single file.

watchPoints.text: Raise The Stakes faces zero pressure on the lead — watch whether Cieren Fallon allows the field to creep into contention or builds an early decisive advantage, as this will determine whether anything can catch the leader at all.

Shabu Shabu and Zafaan are both true hold-up horses effectively forced to race closer to the pace than ideal — watch their early positioning at the break to see whether either can settle just off Raise The Stakes rather than being stuck in the rear cluster.

Mist Of Time shares a trainer with Raise The Stakes; watch for any stable-order dynamic where one horse is ridden to assist the other, which could affect how aggressively either is ridden in the straight.

The going is confirmed Good To Firm for this race despite the official Going listed as Good — watch how horses handle the faster surface, particularly the three 3yos who have limited experience of quick ground and may not handle the kickback at Yarmouth.

Hunting Berries, Ibiza Lights and Mist Of Time all carry fade flags — if any of these move prominently in the early stages, watch for them to weaken significantly in the final furlong and potentially impede hold-up horses attempting to challenge late.

races.name: QuinnBet Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Red Hat Eagle
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with course experience on Good ground; Curtis Wilson-Ruddock claims 7lb which tempers confidence slightly, but the horse has placed on similar going at 8f and steps back to a more suitable 7f wearing headgear; 8 days since last run is ideal freshness.

runners_data.name: Rogue Allegiance
runners_data.note: Harry Davies takes the ride on this consistent hold-up performer who has placed four times in five recent starts on Good ground at 6-7f; 37 days since last run is not alarming but will need the race to develop strongly enough for a late challenge to materialise.

runners_data.name: Mister Mojito
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa brings significant class to the partnership, and on paper this horse prefers to race prominently, but with Kimbara and Red Hat Eagle already occupying those slots, he is likely to find himself shuffled into midfield against his natural instincts — a scenario that will reduce his impact if the pace stays moderate.

runners_data.name: Exotic Baby
runners_data.note: George Boughey's yard has been in decent form (3/27 over 14 days) and this 3yo filly holds prominent headgear form, though her only comparable Good ground run produced just 11th at 8f; Jack Callan's 3lb claim helps, but limited evidence on fast ground over this trip makes her an unknown quantity.

runners_data.name: Raging Raj
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes over on this lightly-raced 3yo who has placed on Good ground at 8f and won at 7f on Standard going; there is a step down in OR since his last run at 8f and a return to 7f could suit him well in what is a winnable classified field.

runners_data.name: Generous Rascal
runners_data.note: Sean Levey pilots this consistent 3yo who has placed five times from six starts without winning; his best form has come at 6f on Standard and Soft going, and this step up to 7f on Good to Firm ground introduces a question mark, though his prominence in the early stages could see him plugging on for a place.

runners_data.name: Kimbara
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne partners this confirmed front-runner for an in-form Richard Spencer yard (4/12 over 14 days); all four starts have come on Good ground at 6-7f and her placed effort at 7f on Good shows she handles this trip, with the uncontested lead here her clear advantage.

runners_data.name: Ecclefechan
runners_data.note: Stevie Donohoe partners this 3yo whose natural preference is for a hold-up role from the rear, but with multiple hold-up types in the field, he will likely find himself racing in midfield rather than settling deeply — a position from which his 34-day absence and predominantly Standard-ground form make winning difficult.

races.paceDynamic: Kimbara is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger likely to press her hard from the gates, she should control the pace from a relatively comfortable position through the first half of this 7f contest at Yarmouth. The going is Good to Firm throughout the card, which will keep the pace honest but not extreme, meaning Kimbara can dictate a measured gallop and resist rivals across her flanks. Red Hat Eagle and Raging Raj are the likeliest horses to push into prominent positions behind her, creating a mid-sized chasing group without dramatically lifting the tempo. This race shape strongly favours a prominent or pace-pressing profile — a horse sitting just off Kimbara's shoulder or within two lengths of the lead can pounce before the hold-up horses generate momentum. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position: Mister Mojito and Ecclefechan are genuinely prominent and hold-up horses respectively but are mapped to midfield positions they are unlikely to claim naturally, with Kimbara and Red Hat Eagle the most likely to actually secure the early lead and prominent berths.

scenarios.body: If Kimbara leads at a sensible Good-to-Firm clip and horses just off the pace pounce inside the final furlong.

scenarios.body: If the pace stays genuinely steady and no presser can quicken past her in the straight.

scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Closers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If Red Hat Eagle or Raging Raj pushes the pace hard early and drags the race into a genuine test of stamina.
scenarios.body: If Red Hat Eagle or Raging Raj pushes the pace hard early and drags the race into a genuine test of stamina.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Upset, Wide-Margin Closer
scenarios.trigger: If the race becomes a rough early scramble for prominent positions and unexpectedly burns through the field, leaving true backmarkers to pick up pieces.
scenarios.body: If the race becomes a rough early scramble for prominent positions and unexpectedly burns through the field, leaving true backmarkers to pick up pieces.

watchPoints.text: Kimbara's price may shorten significantly at the off given her uncontested lead: if she drifts noticeably in the market, watch for a strong presser like Raging Raj or Red Hat Eagle attracting professional support.

Mister Mojito's redistribution to midfield is the key tactical risk — if De Sousa forces him forward regardless, the early pace order changes completely and could compromise Kimbara's rhythm in the first two furlongs.

Rogue Allegiance has four consecutive places on Good ground at 6-7f but has not won in those starts; if the pace fails to develop strongly enough, her hold-up style will leave her with too much ground to make up on the Yarmouth straight.

Exotic Baby's lack of Good ground form over this trip (one run, finishing 11th at 8f on Good) is worth monitoring — if the going plays faster than expected on the 7f course, her jumping-up-in-trip profile could be exposed.

Generous Rascal's trainer Dylan Cunha has saddled two winners from 25 runners in the past 14 days: a yard showing moderate-but-active form whose runner should not be ignored if money comes for him before the off.

races.name: QuinnBet Daily Free Bet Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Sahana
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for David Simcock who has finished placed in four of five recent starts and was placed on good ground at 8f; drops to 6f here which is likely her minimum trip, and the lack of strong pace makes it harder for her to produce a sustained late run.

runners_data.name: Cameley Days
runners_data.note: Won twice on good going over 5f and placed over 6f earlier in the season; wears headgear and Silvestre De Sousa rides, but 21 days between runs is fine and the concern is whether a slow pace over 6f at Yarmouth gives her enough to chase down from her natural rear position.

runners_data.name: Fantasy Obsessor
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's filly is a genuine hold-up horse by nature, placed twice recently at 5f on soft and standard; shown in midfield on the map because the field is stacked with closers, meaning she is effectively racing out of her preferred rear position and that compromises her chance if she cannot get back.

runners_data.name: Egotistical
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's three-year-old is the key pace influence, having won over this course and distance on good ground and landed in the top three in four of five starts; Jack Mitchell's tactical awareness when given a clear lead is a positive, and the uncontested front makes this her race to lose.

runners_data.name: Always Perfect
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes' three-year-old has been placed in half her starts and is tactically versatile enough to track the leader, which is a genuine advantage when the pace is controlled; Paddy Bradley claims 5lbs and the horse's consistent proximity in running suits a shape where she simply needs to latch onto Egotistical's slipstream.

runners_data.name: Q T Pie
runners_data.note: Non-runner — no further assessment applies.

races.paceDynamic: Egotistical is the confirmed front-runner here and, with Q T Pie a non-runner, faces minimal genuine early pressure from the remaining five runners, all of whom sit in hold-up or prominent-but-not-aggressive profiles. Egotistical under Jack Mitchell for Roger Varian has won over this course and distance on good ground and will stride into a clear lead from the off, controlling tempo on a fair surface that will reward whoever gets first run. The field behind her is dominated by hold-up types — Sahana, Cameley Days, and Fantasy Obsessor all want to come from off the pace — meaning the closers will be chasing the same piece of ground in the final two furlongs with no one pressuring the leader through the early stages. This race shape strongly favours the lone front-runner who can dictate a sustainable gallop and then accelerate clear, with hold-up horses vulnerable if the pace is not truly strong enough to bring them into it late. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate cleanly; Fantasy Obsessor is a genuine rear-of-field horse shown in midfield and is unlikely to secure a truly prominent position from which to challenge.

scenarios.title: Egotistical Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Egotistical bowls straight to the front and sets a measured, uncontested gallop that denies the hold-up horses a true test pace.
scenarios.body: If Egotistical bowls straight to the front and sets a measured, uncontested gallop that denies the hold-up horses a true test pace.

scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Reel In
scenarios.trigger: If Egotistical sets a stronger gallop than expected, leaving the door ajar for the closers in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Egotistical sets a stronger gallop than expected, leaving the door ajar for the closers in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle Late
scenarios.trigger: If Always Perfect tracks Egotistical closely and mounts a sustained challenge inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Always Perfect tracks Egotistical closely and mounts a sustained challenge inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp Them All
scenarios.trigger: If a surprisingly brisk early pace collapses the front-runner and a wall of hold-up horses sweeps through.
scenarios.body: If a surprisingly brisk early pace collapses the front-runner and a wall of hold-up horses sweeps through.

watchPoints.text: Egotistical (Jack Mitchell) — watch for her being allowed to coast in front; if Mitchell gets a soft lead and sets only a fair gallop, the hold-up horses may simply not generate enough closing speed to catch her.
Sahana — watch her position at halfway; if Sean Bowen is forced to push up earlier than ideal because the pace is too slow, she risks burning her finishing kick before the final furlong arrives.

Cameley Days — watch whether De Sousa positions her closer than usual given the absence of genuine pace; if she tracks midfield rather than off the back, she becomes a more dangerous proposition in the final 100 yards.

Fantasy Obsessor — watch her early berth out of the stalls; Cieren Fallon will need to decide almost immediately whether to push forward or settle for the back, and in a small field of six she may end up more prominent than her form suggests is natural.

Always Perfect — watch her stride pattern as the field turns into the final two furlongs; if she is sitting second and Egotistical has not quickened away, the Fellowes filly at a career-low weight of 128lbs could be more dangerous than her market position implies.

races.name: quinnbet.com Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Coolagh Magic
runners_data.note: Veteran 10-year-old who has been in reasonable recent form (4th, 3rd in recent starts) and handles Good ground adequately; a genuine hold-up horse in nature but shifted to midfield in the map as the rear is oversubscribed, which slightly reduces the benefit of his typical style in a race that likely won't generate enough pace for him to aim at.

runners_data.name: Sir Rodneyredblood
runners_data.note: 59 days off the track for J R Jenkins (T14: 0/4) is an immediate fitness flag, and he has shown only three placed efforts from 15 similar-going runs without a win; his hold-up style is his natural mode but the lack of a genuine pace to chase on this trip and the long absence combine to dampen his prospects significantly.

runners_data.name: Valadero
runners_data.note: Returning after a lengthy 165-day break for Brian Toomey, who has sent out 0 winners from 2 recent runners — the fitness question is substantial; races over 7-8f as a natural distance and is stepping back to 6f, and while he is a genuine hold-up type, his recent all-Stansted form on Standard ground translates poorly to Good to Firm Yarmouth conditions.

runners_data.name: Bear Steps
runners_data.note: Three-year-old from Jack Jones whose yard has sent out 2 winners from 10 runners over the past fortnight, giving some trainer form; shows a hold-up profile in the data but his historical runs at Yarmouth-type tracks suggest he can press forward, making him one of the horses most likely to grab an uncontested lead if bold from the gate — the jockey booking of Cieren Fallon adds class.

runners_data.name: Shining Guest
runners_data.note: George Margarson's three-year-old brings the best jockey in the race in Silvestre De Sousa, whose positional awareness is a key asset when the entire race becomes a 2f sprint; the limited form string (6th, 7th, 6th) offers modest evidence but all runs are on Good ground at 6-7f, making this the most course-and-conditions-relevant profile in the field.

runners_data.name: Wondrous
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish, which is an acute concern in a race that is almost certain to be decided by a sprint from the 2f pole; Michael Bell's yard is 1 from 21 over 14 days and the horse was last seen finishing 9th over 8f Good, suggesting neither the trip nor the form trajectory inspires confidence, despite being well-matched on official ratings.

races.paceDynamic: This is a six-runner field at Yarmouth over 6f on Good to Firm ground where every single runner carries a hold-up profile — there is no natural front-runner and no confirmed pace-setter in the field. With no horse willing to lead, the early gallop is likely to be pedestrian, with the field drifting through the first two furlongs before the race ignites into a sprint from the 2f pole. That compressed, end-loaded shape typically favours horses with the sharpest turn of foot in the closing stages, but critically every runner here is tagged as a hold-up type, meaning the "sprint finish" dynamic is universal and the race will be decided by who shows the most acceleration from a near-identical position. The field holds more hold-up types than can logically be separated at the rear — Bear Steps, Valadero, Coolagh Magic, and Sir Rodneyredblood are redistributed to midfield because the race map cannot place them all at the back — with Shining Guest and Wondrous the most genuinely natural hold-up operators in this shape. Given no pace source exists, the tactical verdict favours horses with the highest cruising speed who can take a good position from a standstill and sustain a finish, rather than true deep closers who need a genuine pace to aim at.

watchPoints.text: Shining Guest — Silvestre De Sousa is the standout jockey booking in what will be a split-second sprint finish, and he is capable of producing a winning ride from any position in a race with no genuine pace.

Bear Steps — watch for a bold break from the gate; in a field of true hold-up horses, any runner willing to stride to the front unchallenged could steal a significant advantage before the others react.
Valadero — 165 days off the track with a trainer showing 0 from 2 recent runners is a significant welfare and fitness concern; watch for signs of under-readiness in the paddock and early running.

Wondrous — the "fades in finish" flag is critical in a race almost guaranteed to end in a sprint; if the horse cannot sustain its effort over the final furlong on Good to Firm ground, it will be quickly passed by the field at a decisive moment.

Sir Rodneyredblood — 59 days off the track and 0 wins from 15 similar-going runs; worth monitoring whether jockey Jonny Peate attempts to adopt a more prominent position to compensate for the lack of natural pace in the race.
